questions.prompt: After the kernel is established, what question does Chapter 6 add?
choices: Where strategic power comes from
How to write more goals
How to measure effort
questions.explanation: Chapter 6 shifts from structure to force by asking where power comes from.

questions.prompt: Which option best describes a source of power in this chapter?
choices: Any team working very hard
A condition that changes what one move is worth
A slogan that keeps morale high
questions.explanation: A source of power is some condition or asymmetry that changes the odds and the value of action.

questions.prompt: Why can copying a rival's visible tactic fail?
choices: Because imitation is always unethical
Because copied tactics always cost too much
Because the underlying source of power may not have been copied
questions.explanation: The visible move may be only the carrier while the real source of power sits underneath in a deeper condition.

questions.prompt: In the school examples, what should a leader look for before demanding more effort?
choices: The condition that changes the odds
The largest budget line
The most energetic slogan
questions.explanation: The chapter treats the force-generating condition as more important than raw volume or enthusiasm.

questions.prompt: Which apparent advantage is least likely to count as durable power?
choices: A position that keeps strengthening later moves
A one-time trick before the field answers
A fit that makes ordinary action more valuable
questions.explanation: One-time surprise is not the same as durable power because it may disappear after first contact.

questions.prompt: How does Chapter 6 relate to Chapter 2 on leverage?
choices: It rejects leverage as too abstract
It says leverage comes only from effort
It says power must be located before leverage is applied
questions.explanation: Chapter 6 tightens the sequence by locating force first so leverage can later be used well.

questions.prompt: A household plan keeps adding hours but never gets easier. What is the chapter likely to ask next?
choices: What condition would make one move stronger than another?
How can the family add more goals?
Which person can work the most weekends?
questions.explanation: The chapter redirects attention from brute effort to the condition that would actually change the odds.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest sign that an apparent edge is real power?
choices: It survives response and keeps changing the value of action
It sounds impressive in the meeting
It creates more activity across every front
questions.explanation: Durable power continues to matter after response; it is not just dramatic at first sight.

questions.prompt: Why can a strategy have a sound kernel and still remain weak?
choices: Because the leader wrote too little
Because coherence alone does not guarantee a source of power
Because policy always weakens action
questions.explanation: Diagnosis, policy, and coherent action can all be present while the plan still lacks a force-generating condition.

questions.prompt: What chapter move naturally follows identifying a source of power?
choices: Turning to the use of leverage
Returning to generic mission language
Adding more activity before choosing a line
questions.explanation: Once power is located, the next question becomes how leverage should be used against it.
